headline: Medium prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks arise from shared file/clipboard workflows between ChatGPT Desktop and kotaemon.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can read files, clipboard, screenshots, and supported-app content, while kotaemon ingests documents and chat transcripts via a web UI. If content moves from kotaemon into ChatGPT through copy/paste or shared files, attacker-controlled text can be treated as instructions. The pair lacks documented provenance controls, so the interaction is plausible in default workflows.
conditions: IF the operator copies kotaemon-generated text into ChatGPT Desktop
IF both agents access the same document via a shared file or app bridge
mitigations: Use a strict copy/paste policy for untrusted text
Separate workspaces so the same file is not opened in both agents
Add a manual instruction-vs-data delimiter before pasting
Disable clipboard bridging during review sessions
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between the two UIs

B_data_leakage.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, and kotaemon handles documents plus API keys in ./ktem_app_data. If the same sensitive document is opened in both, either agent can expose it through its own backend calls or logs. The profiles do not show isolation between their file surfaces, so leakage is plausible without extra controls.
conditions: IF the same sensitive file is placed in both agents' reachable folders
IF kotaemon is configured to process documents containing secrets or regulated data
mitigations: Keep secrets out of shared document folders
Store sensitive inputs in a separate, access-controlled directory
Review kotaemon uploads before indexing
Avoid sending screenshots or voice containing secrets to ChatGPT Desktop
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop cannot write the filesystem or modify git state, while kotaemon's profile only shows a web UI and a local data directory. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. Some overlap remains on shared documents and API-backed outputs, but the profiles do not show both agents mutating the same resource by default.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory
IF the operator manually syncs their outputs into one mutable repo
mitigations: Keep one agent read-only for shared artifacts
Use separate output folders
Avoid concurrent edits to the same repo
Check for accidental overwrites before saving
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop can produce synthesized answers from files and app context, and kotaemon is a RAG-style support system that can consume documents and citations. If kotaemon treats ChatGPT output as authoritative, errors can cascade from one model into the other and then into user-facing answers. No verification step is documented in either profile, so the pathway exists in default workflows.
conditions: IF kotaemon ingests ChatGPT-generated text as source material
IF the operator uses ChatGPT output as a citation or fact source in kotaemon
mitigations: Require human verification before reusing model output
Mark AI-generated text as non-authoritative in the workflow
Cross-check citations against original documents
Limit kotaemon ingestion to primary sources only
requires-engineering: add source-trust scoring

E_compliance.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop is documented as handling uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while kotaemon handles documents and API keys in a local data directory. If regulated or residency-bound data is routed through both, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not show matching compliance controls, so the safest reading is a medium mismatch risk.
conditions: IF EU PII or regulated documents are processed through both agents
IF retention or deletion obligations differ between the two deployments
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through both systems
Document retention settings for each agent
Purge temporary uploads after use
Restrict kotaemon to non-sensitive corpora
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
